replacement: From the end of 1811, Western Europe armed and massed its forces more and more intensely, and in 1812 those forces — millions of men, counting the ones who carried supplies and fed the army — set out from the west and moved east toward the Russian frontier. Since 1811 the Russian forces had been drawn toward that same frontier. On the twelfth of June, 1812, the forces of Western Europe crossed it and war began. In other words, something happened that ran against human reason and human nature. Millions of men committed against one another countless crimes, frauds, betrayals, thefts, forgeries, issues of counterfeit money, burglaries, arsons, and murders — more than the records of all the law courts in the world could hold in whole centuries — and at the time the men who committed them did not regard them as crimes.
